payload.pattern: Capability discovery lies in BOTH directions: false-MISSING (map not federated) and false-READY (presence != scope). CANON-019 mandates check-secrets before declaring a blocker — so the gate manufactures the phantom blockers it exists to prevent.
payload.solution: Vorn S305 root-fixed both halves. (1) FALSE-MISSING: scripts/lib/secrets.mjs loadCapMap() read CAPABILITY_MAP.json ONLY from <repo>/secrets/, while loadEnv() federated KEYS to the studio-ops gateway. Any sibling repo with no local secrets/ (Vorn has none by design) resolved against an EMPTY map, so check-secrets reported MISSING for 100% of capabilities — 0/65 rendered as 0/0 ready. A made-up capability returned byte-identical output to a real one. Fix: federate the map on the same low->high precedence contract as keys (ops -> local, local overrides). Vorn went 0/0 -> 40/65 ready. (2) DESIGN: resolveCapability collapsed known-but-uncredentialed and unknown-to-map into one ok:false, which is what turns a map gap into a founder escalation. Added a third state: {known, state: ready|partial|missing|unknown, mapUnresolved}; check-secrets renders UNKNOWN distinctly, exit 2 (still non-zero, so existing not-ready callers are unchanged) and never routes UNKNOWN to Human Action Required. An unresolvable map is now LOUD — S180 had marked absent-map benign as a CI edge case, but for a sibling repo it is the permanent production state, so the one failure mode that actually occurs had no signal. (3) FALSE-READY (the S304 follow-up): scripts/capability-scope-probe.mjs verifies a stored credential holds the SCOPE it was stored for, not merely that it exists. Live proof: CLOUDFLARE_DNS_TOKEN reads READY but resolves only vaultsparkstudios.com, never joinvorn.com — reproducing S304 hand-diagnosis automatically. Probe can only DOWNGRADE a READY; it reports skipped/unknown rather than fabricating a pass.
payload.proposal: Control plane should (a) federate loadCapMap in the canonical secrets.mjs so no sibling repo silently resolves an empty map, (b) adopt the three-state resolver contract so UNKNOWN can never be escalated as MISSING, and (c) carry optional scope declarations in CAPABILITY_MAP.json (e.g. cloudflare.dns -> expect zone joinvorn.com) so readiness = presence AND scope, checked periodically portfolio-wide. Scope decls intentionally NOT added to the ops map from here — CANON-018 forbids sibling tree edits; this is the proposal.

payload.pattern: A consumer with a PRIVATE regex over a canonical file it does not own will silently outlive its producers format — and it fails to CONFIDENT GREEN, never to an error. Obelisk: 9 parsers read its context files, 2 used the shared reader. The SIL forecaster demanded an em-dash the file stopped using 53 sessions (15 days) ago; it hoisted a 12-day-old entry to index 0 and rendered it as current, because a PARTIAL parse is non-empty and therefore plausible. One render pass printed 994/1000 and vs current 1000 — same file, same fact, two parsers, two answers. Elsewhere the same class made a whole brief box VANISH (it hunted a heading deleted waves ago) while 6 founder blockers sat unrendered, made a preflight report 2 of 9 as a complete count, and left a prune-on-empty that would have wiped an entire ledger on every startup.
payload.solution: 1) ONE canonical file, ONE parser — delete private regexes, import the owner. 2) THREE-STATE COVERAGE: a parser must be able to say I cannot see the present (complete/partial/blind); if the newest heading in the file is not the newest thing the parser sees, no consumer may render a confident current from it. 3) Bind the test to the LIVE file, not a fixture — a fixture agrees with the parser, so it only proves the code agrees with itself (coherence is not correspondence). 4) An empty parse must NEVER authorize a prune/delete — require positive evidence the source was actually read. 5) Ship a STANDING SWEEP gate, because the deepest lesson is that we diagnosed this class TWICE (W91, W204), wrote the lesson in a comment both times, and cured only the instance in front of us — W204s fix sits 20 lines from the import of the parser carrying the identical bug. THE CURE MUST BE APPLIED TO THE CLASS, NOT THE INSTANCE, or it ships again.

portable_lessons: THE FOURTH QUESTION — S223 asked which GATES have no caller; S224 which CLAIMS have no reader; S225 which ENDS disagree; S226 asks WHICH CLAIMS OF A MECHANISM HAVE NONE. Every finding was that shape: a heading reading 'Rolling Status (auto-updated each closeout)' that nothing auto-updates (4 closeouts stale, and the brief reads it for the founder's Runway signal); a working CANON-031 enforcer with a --check CLI that no lane ever called; a TRUTH_AUDIT entry naming a producer deleted three sessions earlier. A title is not a mechanism. Portable check: scripts/check-generated-claims.mjs — every artifact claiming 'I am generated by X' must prove X exists.

A GATE INVISIBLE TO THE GATE MAP — write-project-status.mjs enforced silScore := sum(silCategoriesV3) and shipped a working --check, and S223's gate-axis map could not see it because that map enumerates check:* npm scripts and this was not named one. The map carried the blind spot it was built to detect. If your gate map enumerates by NAME, every correctly-built gate with the wrong name is invisible to it.

THE MAP PENALISES THE BETTER CODE — an AST presence-map that only resolves literal property access (v3.devHealth) cannot see a computed one (v3[cat.key]). Refactoring ten duplicated explicit reads into one loop made all ten fields look UNREAD, so the map had been rewarding duplication because duplication is what it could see. Fix: a computed read reports `dynamic`, never `inert` — absence of proof is not proof of absence (D-S222.1 run in reverse). But keep the two ends UNCROSSED: a reader-side fact must never excuse a missing writer.

A LOOKUP TABLE KEYED BY AN OBJECT LITERAL READS AS A PRODUCER — `const LABELS = { devHealth: ... }` is indistinguishable to an AST write-index from `status = { devHealth: 100 }`. Mine forged ten writes and masked five genuine fossils as `live`, making the honesty instrument less honest. Use a Map keyed by string VALUES. A lookup must not read as a producer.

MAKE THE DECLARATION TRUE, THEN DECLARE IT — S225 refused to declare 15 fields because a name-match cannot tell a writer from an aggregator that merely reads our status. The fix was not to relax the standard but to ship the structural resolver: prove the file WRITES the artifact's PATH. And where the declaration was simply false (the closeout template instructed writing the DERIVED total while never naming the SOURCE it must be summed from), the template was corrected FIRST and only then declared. Declaring first and hoping is how a ledger starts lying.

A SCORE PINNED AT MAX IS NOT MEASURING — StatVault's SIL read 1000/1000 for five consecutive sessions (sparkline █████). Forcing the question found two easy deductions: Engagement carries the PRODUCT rubric (Stakeholder Velocity, Community Engagement) on a PRE-LAUNCH project with no users, so it is unanswerable and defaults to 100 by scoring nothing; Ecosystem rewards a cargo SHIPPED identically to a cargo RECEIVED. A rubric that cannot be answered honestly will be answered dishonestly. The SIL is the one instrument no gate audits, because it is the thing the gates report to — every studio project on the v3 rubric should check whether its own score still discriminates.

DERIVE THE DERIVABLE, DATE THE JUDGEMENT — when ratcheting a hand-typed artifact to derived-from-run, some fields are genuinely judgements no artifact can compute (momentum runway, intent rate, debt). Inventing them would be fabricating data to pass a gate. Preserve them and STAMP them with the session they were made in, so a carried-over judgement discloses its own age instead of masquerading as current.

payload.pattern: Phantom remedies: a propagated remedy map advertises fix scripts that do not exist in the receiving repo — and the honesty guard then enforces the lie
payload.context: Any repo that received scripts/lib/doctor-remedies.mjs from studio-ops. The maps name scripts that exist in studio-ops; in an app checkout many do not. Verified live in living-protocol at S264: 11 advertised remedies resolved to absent scripts (last-session-summary, validate, revenue, compliance-velocity, ark-slo, agents-md-drift, analytica-freshness, prompt-ver, consumer-adoption, ark-inbox-depth). payload.solution: Verify self-remediability against the FILESYSTEM instead of asserting it from a map. isSelfRemediable() now resolves the script each path names (including scripts/X.mjs extracted from SELF_REMEDIABLE_NO_AUTOHEAL command strings and REMEDIES labels) and returns false when it is absent from this checkout; fails closed. Correct in BOTH repos by construction: in studio-ops the scripts exist and nothing changes, in an app checkout the truth is told. Paired with findPhantomRemedies() wired as a remedy-honesty doctor probe so a newly-propagated map entry naming an absent script reds immediately instead of drifting. payload.pattern: classify-warning-provenance.mjs is studio-ops-centric but propagated verbatim — in a sibling repo its notion of self is wrong and its evidence engine is silently dead
payload.context: scripts/classify-warning-provenance.mjs is byte-identical across repos, but was authored FOR the control plane: OWN_SLUG is hardcoded to vaultspark-studio-ops and the docstring reasons about whether STUDIO-OPS has debt. Two consequences observed live in living-protocol at S264. (1) loadSiblingSlugs() reads portfolio/PROJECT_REGISTRY.json, which app checkouts do not have, and swallows the miss with catch { return [] } — so suggestOwnerFromEvidence() can never fire and the entire S174 evidence-beats-heuristic upgrade is DEAD CODE in every sibling repo, silently, with no signal that it degraded. resolveSuggestedOwner always falls back to the driftClass heuristic. (2) studio-ops is excluded from the sibling slug list, so in a sibling repo — where studio-ops IS a foreign repo — its warnings can never be evidenced as sibling-owned and collapse to self.
payload.solution: Two asks for studio-ops as the owner. (a) Make the degradation observable rather than silent: an empty slug table is a DEGRADED state that must be reported, not a successful classification — no honesty instrument should fail open and quiet. (b) Generalize the self/sibling vantage: derive OWN_SLUG from the running repo (context/PROJECT_STATUS.json slug) rather than hardcoding the control plane, so self is correct in whichever repo the module runs. living-protocol did NOT patch its local copy — the file is byte-identical to upstream and the root cause is portfolio-wide (~30 repos), so it is shipped as cargo per CANON-018 rather than forked into local drift.

payload.pattern: check-canon-conformance.mjs destroys checker output — it reports the last line of stdout instead of parsing the JSON
payload.context: Verified live at S264 from living-protocol. check-canon-044-waves.mjs emits well-formed JSON ({ok,surfacesChecked,findings:[{file,issue}]}) and exits 1 on a gap. The conformance engine renders that gap as: detail: "}" — literally the closing brace, the last line of the pretty-printed JSON. Every gap detail from a JSON-emitting per-project checker is destroyed the same way, so the founder-facing conformance report shows a real gap with unreadable evidence and the actual finding (which file, which marker) is silently discarded.
payload.solution: Parse the checker stdout as JSON and surface findings[] (file + issue), falling back to the last non-empty line only when the payload is not JSON. payload.pattern: A registry is a source-of-truth for the READ side only when the WRITE side cannot free-string past it. A kind/constant registry that consumers cite but producers bypass with literals is half a cure: a producer typo of a registered kind silently orphans every constant-reading consumer, and no consumer-side gate can show it (instruments-cannot-show-decline).
payload.solution: Guard BOTH directions. Add an emit-side pass to the ownership gate, but PRECISION-scope it (W194): the registry is deliberately limited to CONSUMED kinds (~80 legit unregistered kinds emit in-perimeter), so unregistered-emit=finding over-fires. Flag ONLY a Levenshtein<=2 (len>=5) near-miss of a registered kind (a plausible typo); make exact-registered-literal emits an ADVISORY count (the migrate-to-constant backlog), and let far kinds pass. Also: boolean-may-harden-never-certify binds at EVERY plane that reads the boolean, not just where first cured (readiness scorecard vs brief).

payload.pattern: A self-refreshing gauge whose decline-threshold is INHERITED from a manual-probe SLA is blind for N-times its own cadence
payload.solution: Bind a timer-fed freshness window to the probe cadence (a small multiple), NEVER reuse a manual-sweep SLA constant; export ONE value so the UI stale-threshold == the operator alarm fire-threshold; make the trend recency-aware (a dead timer must not render 100% up); and put the keeper OFF-BOX (probe the live surface, not a build-host snapshot). A standing test asserts window != manualSLA and <= k*cadence so the inheritance cannot return.
